angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 626,826 km at 195.48 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.1157 +/- 0.0096 mas (same row, RUWE 0.75): 195.48 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.901 +/- 0.027 solar radii from Sanchis-Ojeda et al. 2013, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of Kepler-63 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2013ApJ...775...54S/abstract): 626,826 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.984 +/- 0.035 solar masses from Sanchis-Ojeda et al. 2013, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of Kepler-63 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2013ApJ...775...54S/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5576 +/- 50 K from Sanchis-Ojeda et al. 2013, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-63 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2013ApJ...775...54S/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Sanchis-Ojeda et al. 2013, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-63 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2013ApJ...775...54S/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/kepler-63.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.522, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of Kepler-63 (pscomppars): spectral type G5, from Bourrier et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...669A..63B/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of Kepler-63 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.05 dex, from Sanchis-Ojeda et al. 2013 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2013ApJ...775...54S/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of Kepler-63 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.157, from Sanchis-Ojeda et al. 2013 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2013ApJ...775...54S/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of Kepler-63 (pscomppars): age 0.21 Gyr, from Sanchis-Ojeda et al. 2013 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2013ApJ...775...54S/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of Kepler-63 (pscomppars): rotation period 5.401 d, from Bourrier et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...669A..63B/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of Kepler-63 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 5.6 km/s, from Sanchis-Ojeda et al. 2013 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2013ApJ...775...54S/abstract)
spinInclinationSource: Computed here from this record's rotation period, projected rotation speed and radius (0.901 solar radii): sin i = v sin i × P / (2πR) = 0.664. Not a measurement of the axis: the three numbers come from different papers.

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
